issues.description: The template's singFarmSongVerse method is declared without an Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), but the problem UML and the solution expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This parameter mismatch will confuse students implementing the verse printing (they are instructed to use the passed Animal to print the class name and call messageOnFeed()), and the current stub prevents straightforward implementation without editing the method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to include an Animal parameter to match the UML and solution, e.g. private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... } and use that parameter in the method body (animal.getClass().getSimpleName(), animal.messageOnFeed()).

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement indicates singFarmSongVerse is private (prefixed with '-'), the template declares it as private, but the solution implements it as protected. This visibility mismatch between solution and the UML/template may confuse students about the intended visibility and whether overriding or testing access is expected.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent. Either change the solution method to private to match the UML/template, or update the UML/problem text and the template stub to indicate protected visibility. Prefer making the template and UML agree with the chosen visibility so students know the intended access level.
